title: Early accordions in dance bands
summary: He describes small German accordions with natural notes and two basses, and playing with accordion, guitar and bass.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Who played what: early band size and instrumentation

blocks.x: Did you ever have any of those old bands that, a dance band, a dance and jazz band that had an accordion in it? No.

Yeah, accordion, but the accordions that they had at that time, but it's not the accordions. Well, like a concertina I guess is that. No, that's it. It wasn't a concertina. It was a red accordion like they got there. Yeah. But they only had the natural notes. They had no sharps.
No full keyboard. In other words, it ran, I believe it was 16 notes, that's all. In accordion, and they only had two bass.
They had the tonic and the seventh, that's all.
So it was a lot smaller instrument then than what you were saying?
Yeah, well it was no bigger than that, and about that wide, and it stretched out that long. Uh-huh.
Is that like the Cajun Jews? Is that what they call a German accordion?

Yeah, yeah, that's it. The German accordion. I heard of them, but I haven't seen them. That's what they used to have at that time. Yeah. Well, I played with that, with accordion, guitar and bass. I played with accordion.
